podcast.title: Jimmy Osterberg's Band in 1964
podcast.body: In 1964, Jimmy Osterberg (later Iggy Pop) was singing and playing drums for The Iguanas. This band was his primary musical outlet at the time. "Jimmy Osterberg singing and playing the drums for the iguanas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dissolution and Formation of The Psychedelic Stooges (Summer 1967)
podcast.body: The Iguanas disbanded in the summer of 1967, paving the way for Iggy Pop to form his new group, The Psychedelic Stooges. "by that summer, the iguanas were gone and Iggy was in a new band called The Psychedelic Stooges."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Band Experience
podcast.body: The Iguanas were the first band of consequence for James Newell Osterberg (Iggy), where he played as a drummer. They were good enough to open for Motown groups and sometimes served as the backing band for out-of-town acts passing through Detroit. "The first of any consequence was the iguanas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

podcast.title: Early Band for Iggy Pop – Michigan Gigs
podcast.body: The Iguanas were a Detroit-based band for which Iggy Pop served as the drummer in the mid-sixties. They performed gigs around Michigan and recorded a few songs during this period. "He was the drummer for Detroit band called the iguanas and they played gigs around Michigan and even recorded a few songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Blues Focus and Iggy's Name
xref.body: The Prime Movers was a blues band where James Newell Osterberg played as a drummer. It was during his time with this band that he became known as "Iggy," a nickname derived from his previous band, The Iguanas. "Next came the prime movers and they were more of a blues band and here's where Jim became known as Iggy because, well, he used to play in the iguanas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Early Career as a Drummer
xref.body: Before gaining fame as Iggy Pop, James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer in Detroit in the mid-1960s. He backed Motown groups like The Shangri-La's and The Temptations when they played in Michigan, and also played in a local band called The Iguanas. "James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer from Detroit who had spent much of the middle 60s backing up Motown groups like the Shangri-La's and the temptations whenever they played around Michigan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1

xref.title: Early Drumming Career – Motown Gigs
xref.body: In the mid-sixties, Iggy Pop began his musical career as a drummer for the Detroit band The Iguanas, playing gigs around Michigan and recording several songs. He was also hired locally by Motown acts like The Shangri-La's, The Temptations, and The Four Tops for their live gigs, as they toured with minimal musicians and hired bassists and drummers on location. He was known for being able to pick up almost any song within seconds. "Iggy was one of the guys These Motown acts would hire to play drums for them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Iggy Pop's Name Origin
xref.body: James Newell Osterberg adopted the stage name "Iggy" from his previous band, The Iguanas. The "Pop" part was added after he shaved off his eyebrows in a "weird stoned gesture," leading the other band members to comment that he resembled a local drug user named Jim Pop. "The pop part came after Iggy shaved off his eyebrows in some weird stone to gesture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Name Origin - Iggy Pop
xref.body: The name "Iggy" was taken from his first band, The Iguanas, while "Pop" was inspired by a junkie friend named Jim Pop. Jim suffered from a medical condition that caused him to lose all his hair, including his eyebrows, which Iggy thought was "pretty cool," leading him to shave his own eyebrows and cement his new stage name. "Iggy, after the iguanas, and Pop, after a junkie friend named Jim Pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Iggy Pop

xref.title: Origin of Nickname "Iggy"
xref.body: Jimmy Osterberg earned the nickname "Iggy" because he played drums for his band, The Iguanas. "Because he played for the iguanas, he got the nickname Iggy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin of the Name Iggy Pop
xref.body: James Osterberg adopted the stage name Iggy Pop, with "Iggy" derived from his time playing with The Iguanas, and "Pop" taken after a local junkie. "By this time, James was going by the name Iggy Pop, Iggy from his time in the iguanas and pop after a local junkie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
